nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every $p \in [0, 1]$ and every real $t$, the characteristic function $\varphi_{\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)}$ of the binomial distribution $\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$, viewed as a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, satisfies $\varphi_{\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)}(t) = \left((1 - p) + p e^{it}\right)^n$.
nodes.title: Characteristic function of the real-valued binomial distribution

nodes.summary:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $a, s, t \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $
u$ be the image of $\mu$ under the map $x \mapsto (x - a)/s$. Then the characteristic functions satisfy $\varphi_
u(t) = \varphi_\mu(t s^{-1}) \, e^{-i a t s^{-1}}$. Here $s^{-1}$ and division by $s$ are read as $0$ when $s = 0$, so no hypothesis $s 
eq 0$ is needed.
nodes.title: Affine transformation of a characteristic function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every $p \in [0, 1]$ and every real $t$, put $s = \sqrt{np(1-p)}$, with $s^{-1}$ read as $0$ when $s = 0$. Let $\psi$ be the characteristic function of the binomial distribution $\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$ viewed as a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and $\varphi$ that of the standardized binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Then $\varphi(t) = \psi(t s^{-1}) \, e^{-i n p t s^{-1}}$.
nodes.title: Characteristic function of the standardized binomial

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically distributed real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$, each almost surely equal to $0$ or $1$, with mean $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$. Write $S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$. Then for all real numbers $a \le b$, the probability $P\left(a \le (S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)} \le b\right)$ tends, as $n \to \infty$, to the mass that the standard normal distribution…
nodes.title: De Moivre–Laplace limit theorem, interval form

nodes.summary: For a sequence $X_0, X_1, \dots$ of real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, a real number $p$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the standardized partial sum is the function $\omega \mapsto (S_n(\omega) - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ on $\Omega$, where $S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Standardized partial sums

nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically distributed real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$, each almost surely equal to $0$ or $1$, with mean $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$. Write $S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$. Then the standardized sums $(S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ converge in distribution to the standard normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: De Moivre–Laplace limit theorem, convergence in distribution

nodes.summary: For every complex number $z$ with $|z| \le 1$, the remainder after the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of the exponential satisfies $|e^z - 1 - z - z^2/2| \le 2|z|^3$.
nodes.title: Second-order Taylor remainder bound for the exponential

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be almost everywhere measurable with $f(\omega) \in \{0, 1\}$ for $P$-almost every $\omega$. Then $f$ is integrable with respect to $P$.
nodes.title: Almost surely $\{0, 1\}$-valued random variables are integrable

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(\omega) \in \{0, 1\}$ for $P$-almost every $\omega$. Then $\int f^2 \, dP = \int f \, dP$.
nodes.title: Second moment of a $\{0, 1\}$-valued random variable

nodes.summary: For a real number $p$, the standardization map sends $x \in \mathbb{R}$ to $(x - p)/\sqrt{p(1-p)}$.
nodes.title: Bernoulli standardization map

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and $p \in [0, 1]$, the standardized binomial distribution is the measure on $\mathbb{R}$ given by the law of $(S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$, where $S_n$ has the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. When $np(1-p) = 0$ the division by $0$ is read as $0$, so the law is the point mass at $0$.
nodes.title: Standardized binomial distribution

nodes.summary: Let $0 < p < 1$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$. As $n \to \infty$, the characteristic function of the standardized binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$, evaluated at $t$, converges to $e^{-t^2/2}$, the value at $t$ of the characteristic function of the standard normal distribution.
nodes.title: Convergence of characteristic functions in De Moivre–Laplace
